problems_fixed.what: Re-posed a mis-specified problem whose five constraints (mean 12, median 11, mode 10 twice, range 10, smallest 8) were mutually contradictory: no ordered set of five integers satisfies mode 10 (below median) with median 11. Changed median to 10 so a consistent set exists (8, 10, 10, 14, 18), keeping the answer 18. Also replaced the unedited 'Wait/Hmm' internal-monologue misconception with an honest range-vs-largest trap (expect 10).
problems_fixed.old: Five numbers have mean 12 and median 11. The mode is 10 (appears twice). The range is 10. The smallest number is 8. Find all five numbers — what is the largest? (solution 18, contradictory)
problems_fixed.new: Five numbers have a mean of 12, a median of 10 and a mode of 10. The range is 10 and the smallest number is 8. What is the largest number? (solution 18, consistent set 8,10,10,14,18)

opener_concept: Three friends pool pocket money (£2, £4, £9) and share it equally: total 15, split 3 ways = £5. The fair share IS the mean. A student totals and divides by common sense, then the reveal names it as 'add them all up, divide by how many'.
